Netflix has announced that Planeswalker, an animated series based on Magic: The Gathering, will debut in 2027. The first sneak peek doesn't show much, but it does suggest that the show is taking several pages from the streamer's wildly popular League of Legends series, Arcane.

The series "chronicles the fierce clash between formidable mages known as Planeswalkers. At the center of this struggle for power and survival burns Chandra, a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts and haunted by her past," according to the official synopsis.

"Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence. As the line between victory and annihilation grows thinner, a single spark determines the fate of thousands of worlds."

The video above is filled with concept and previsualization clips, but there are a few seconds of what appears to be near-final animation and, well, it's tough to deny a clear Arcane influence here in the character design and animation style. The series is being created by animation studio Digic Pictures, which has previously made cutscenes for games including Assassin's Creed Shadows and Call of Duty: Vanguard, and led several episodes of Amazon's Secret Level series.

Terry Matalas, who served as showrunner for VisionQuest and seasons 2 and 3 of Star Trek: Picard, will be showrunner for Planeswalker. Cindy Appel, who wrote episodes for both those shows, serves as co-showrunner. Patrick Osborne is supervising director and executive producer.

Netflix has been trying to get a Magic: The Gathering series underway since at least 2019, when the streamer announced that the Russo brothers were attached to the project. Whatever vision they had for the series seemingly fell through, as it was five years before we heard about it again – this time, led by Matalas.

In the meantime, check out our guides to the best shows on Netflix and the best movies on Netflix to find out what you should be streaming today.

Mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each update may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major update. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Last but not least, the planned April update will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

#3795. Dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever get a huge XP buff, but power-levellers shouldn't celebrate just yet

World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.

This buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons. As detailed in this World of Warcraft forum post, community manager Kaivax wrote that this change has been made "so it feels better to go back in for more runs". They don't outright say this is in response to community feedback, but the subject has been a hot topic since the beta.

World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons. The idea was that by doing this, people would be encouraged to actually go out into the world and explore it, rather than hopping from instance to instance until they reached max level.

Sadly, a side effect of this change is that doing a dungeon more than once could feel unrewarding. Playing it once is great, as you get to complete lots of quests that reward guaranteed items and XP. However, if you go back again, you don't get these, so your only source of progression comes from a heavily decreased XP rate.

Some quests exacerbate this issue. Dungeons like Wailing Caverns and especially Blackfathom Deeps have a quest that can't really be completed in one run due to a reliance on drop rates for items you need, and having to fight for drops with the rest of your dungeon party. Having to go back to complete this used to suck, and now it sucks less!

So does this mean farming dungeons to power-level is back? Maybe, but it still won't be nearly as efficient as it was in older versions of Classic WoW. The current mob XP rates, after this buff, will still only be 36 percent of the original Classic rate - a third. Given how fast you can level by doing quests out in the world, it seems dungeon farming isn't due for a comeback just yet.

After an especially smooth launch, World of Warcraft: Forever has become the biggest launch in the series' history, beating out Wrath of the Lich King, Cataclysm, and all the other past expansion launches. The developers have been quick to hotfix things on the fly, including a change that left PvP battlegrounds heavily advantaged for the Horde.

AI-enabled hacking is only continuing to get more impressive, and more scary, as a French bank claims a hacking group has cost it €100,000,000 (around $110,000,000)—about one quarter's profits. So not much, then?

That's according to an interview with Julien Carmona of Crédit Mutuel Arkéa with the AFP, which Boursorama reported. Carmona detailed the hack in an interview, claiming it to be a "heist of a new kind", stating the company has the "dubious honor of being the first French bank, and I believe the first European bank, to be the target of a successful fraudulent attack." (machine translated).

Carmona says the hack is "unprecedented in terms of sophistication" and "technicality".

Effectively, the hacking group managed to create fake IBANs, including those from Fortuneo (a bank owned by the group), "to trigger payment orders from Crédit Mutuel Arkea's own account to external parties using instant payment systems". These, "by definition have fewer controls than on classic transfers."

Carmona did clarify to Les Echos that though they use Fortuneo IBANs, "Fortuneo's system, and therefore its customers, were not affected."

‼️ AI-enabled hackers pulled about €100 million out of French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's own account.Its chair, Julien Carmona, told AFP how. The attackers took material from a hacked supplier, used it to get into the bank and generated fake IBANs at its online bank Fortuneo.… pic.twitter.com/fduRERezPWNovember 13, 2026

Reportedly, the hacking group used a compromised service provider of some kind to get privileged access, thereby bypassing restrictions normally in place to stop this kind of hack. When asked by Les Echos why they didn't reveal the name, Carmona said, "This is a collective decision by the banks. This information is not in the public interest and could harm the security of the banking sector. Similar service providers could then be targeted."

Starting on Sunday, November 1, the hacking group apparently made sure "everything was done to circumvent controls, to make these illegitimate transfers appear legitimate."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

They then transferred the funds to legitimate European banks, where they then took that money and spent it on crypto platforms. This hack wasn't spotted until Tuesday, November 3, when access to the bank's information system was cut off, but by that point the damage was done.

The French bank has since brought in crypto specialists, who reportedly spotted the abnormal transaction on Sunday and Monday "But, at that time, they themselves, and no one to my knowledge, made the link with Crédit Mutuel Arkea".

Carmona says the hacking organisation was "a very well-organised, very well-equipped criminal group" and "very likely aided by advanced artificial intelligence."

It's not yet clear what role AI played here, but it's particularly good at analysing data, and of course has found value in coding over the last year. AI was only recently used by a cyberhacking gang to target 60 firms a few months ago. In this Korean case, though, the gang only managed to make $210 in ransom payments before being caught.

Xenoblade series developer Monolith Soft and Bandai Namco Studios have been listed as support studios for the Switch 2 version of Ocarina of Time, working on elements of the title such as "art, including characters, terrain, animations, cutscenes and UI". Special thanks to both companies appear in the credits for the newly-launched game (as you can see below) and a statement released by Bandai Namco Studios confirms its involvement, too.

"We were commissioned to produce some of the visual assets and artwork, including characters, environments, animations, cutscenes, and UI elements, for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, a Nintendo Switch 2 game released by Nintendo Co., Ltd. on 5th November, 2026," reads a translated release from Bandai Namco Studio reads.

Of course, this isn't the first time we've seen Bandai Namco Studios' talents leveraged to help with Nintendo games: the publisher and its internal studios worked closely with Nintendo as a co-developer on the long-awaited Metroid Prime 4, and we know the studios are listed as co-developer for first-party Switch 2 titles like Mario Kart World and Splatoon Raiders. Typically, the work carried out by Bandai Namco comes from one of two dedicated internal studios that are contracted specifically to work with Nintendo: Studio 2 and Studio S. You can see a full list of the games Bandai Namco's support studios have worked on here. You'll note there are many Nintendo first-party titles listed here, going back to 2012 and Mario Kart 8. In late 2025, Nintendo acquired Bandai Namco Studios Singapore from the publisher, renaming the company Nintendo Studios Singapore.

"Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve," wrote our reviewer, Christian Donlan, in his five-star review of the Switch 2 game last week. "This is Ocarina as it's always been, as timeless and intricate, but it also has a vibrancy and clarity that makes it feel like it was just created last Wednesday."

If - somehow! - you've already gobbled up most of the game and you're keen to play it again, you will be pleased to know that Master Quest code has been found in datamined files for the title, suggesting DLC may well be on the way in the not-too-distant future.

Somehow, some way, the PS5 has been an extraordinary sales success despite launching in the middle of a global pandemic that caused massive supply chain issues and continuing on today amidst an unprecedented memory shortage and economic headwinds driving hardware prices sky high. Despite it all, people are buying PS5s, and many of them.

Sony confirmed just this week that PS5 has hit an incredible milestone of 100 million units sold in its six years on the market. That's not quite as fast as the PS2 or PS4, but it's a much more impressive achievement when you consider one crucial difference between the current-gen PlayStation and literally every other generation before it. Typically, games consoles decrease in price throughout their life cycles, but because of the disadvantages outlined above, the PS5 has only gotten more expensive, right alongside its competitors, the Xbox Series X/S and Nintendo Switch 2.

So, even though the PS5 failed to hit 100 million units sold faster than its predecessors, it still reached the record for units sold without any sort of permanent price cut from Sony. And before you head to the comments section to point out that you got a PS5 at a discount for Black Friday one year, we're talking about official, permanent price decreases from Sony, not temporary sales from retailers. That is seriously impressive considering the economic difficulties not only Sony and other hardware manufacturers are grappling with today, but consumers as well.

You could almost, almost make the case for PS5 being the first console period to hit that sales milestone without a price cut, but for the mighty Nintendo Switch. The Switch hit 100 million units sold in December 2021, and Nintendo never lowered its price globally. There was a price cut in Europe in September 2021, notably just before the Switch reached 100 million units, but it doesn't feel fair disqualifying it from claiming Sony's title for a small, regional price decrease alone.

#3788. Skyrim lead designer hopes Sentinel will finally solve The Elder Scrolls' ladder problem

For such a simple, straightforward real-world object, ladders have been the bane of game developers' existence since the early days of the industry. And Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls Series is certainly no stranger to that struggle.

While we may be years away from the release of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the recent title reveal reignited conversations about what longtime fans hope to see from it. That includes former Bethesda developers, such as Skyrim lead designer and Bethesda veteran Bruce Nesmith, who picked ladders as one thing he hopes Sentinel actually figures out.

If you're unfamiliar, ladders in Skyrim work in a weird way. You don't animatedly climb up and down them, but rather the character simply teleports from one end to the other. Speaking to The Examined Game (via GamesRadar+), Nesmith said that Skyrim's approach "really limits the art team in terms of how you can do multi-layer [levels]".

"It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders," said Nesmith. "All the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, poof, you're at the top or you have to climb a stair.

"But to do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions which our programmers very legitimately put in front of us and said, 'You give me answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's going to take to make them.' And you know, that caused problems right there."

Nesmith then pointed out the hidden complexity of creating functioning ladders in games, and the scenarios developers have to anticipate and account for, especially in a game as dynamic as an Elder Scrolls title.

"So, I'm halfway up a ladder, and [an] NPC decides to climb down it. What happens?" Nesmith posited. "The NPC has to have AI that will adjust for that. Does the player go through the NPC? Is he blocked by the NPC? Does the NPC stay on the ladder? Does the NPC go back up and know to wait and then come back down?

"And I'm just scratching the surface of some of the problems they brought up. So, it seems simple, and other games have climbing ladders, but we chose to put our efforts into other things to make them better rather than deal with that. So, I'd like to see Bethesda finally come around to making ladders a reality where you're actually climbing them and make the world feel a little more immersive."

While we know very little about Sentinel right now - much less how it's going to solve the ladder problem -that hasn't stopped fans from speculating about a number of topics, including what they believe is going to be a split / alternate timeline setup.

#3787. Nintendo's legendary Kirby designer Masahiro Sakurai weighs in on gen-AI, saying "it has yet to gain my trust" but not to reject it completely

"Doing nothing is probably not the right approach."

Masahiro Sakurai, the designer behind many iconic Nintendo franchises such as Super Smash Bros. and several Kirby titles, has weighed in on the ongoing discussion of generative-AI use in game development.

At an event celebrating the release of his new book - Masahiro Sakurai’s Thoughts on Games - the veteran director told Famitsu he hasn't and currently isn't using the technology to make games, noting that the role of a designer is to generate ideas.

"It has yet to gain my trust," Sakurai said via DeepL machine translation. Regarding graphical use specifically, he added that, "It must not amount to exploitation of any kind," and that "for the time being, we can produce better results by coming up with ideas ourselves".

But Sakurai is wary of rejecting gen-AI completely, saying "making games today is far too difficult", with some games "running at a loss even after selling millions of copies". A company in that position may go under if it does not change its stance on generative-AI, he suggested. "Doing nothing is probably not the right approach," he said, but "where and how to use it" is a complex topic with a lot of uncertainties. Sakurai is taking "a slow-paced approach" for now.

Outside of regular industry layoffs, the use of generative-AI in games has been the most controversial topic amongst developers and players. Some argue it's already being used in multiple development disciplines, notably programming and writing code. Others, such as Shigeru Miyamoto, are more sceptical of the technology's capabilities, especially when it comes to the more creative and art-driven parts of game development.

"Physical" copies of GTA 6 started shipping out to early buyers this week, including several members of GamesRadar+ staff. As players start to worry that their codes may be stolen with a bizarre flashlight trick, we had to see if we could steal our own – and honestly, I wouldn't be too worried about the possibility.

Rockstar's approach to its code-in-box release of GTA 6 is slightly different from most publishers. Rather than including the game code printed on a slip of paper in the case, the code is printed inside the back cover art itself. Social media is starting to be washed over with reports that if you shine a very bright flashlight just right into the edge of a GTA 6 case, you can make out the code without even breaking the seal on the game.

I tried the trick with my own US copy of the PS5 physical edition, and it did not work. There's a strip of camouflage patterning underneath the code that renders it unreadable from the opposite side no matter how bright a light you shine at it. My colleague Catherine tried the trick with her UK PS5 copy, and same deal – the code is unreadable through that camo pattern.

There is a catch here: not every code-in-box copy of GTA 6 has the camo strip. I've combed through unboxing videos of the game, and while I can't find any examples of US copies without the protective camouflage, some copies with a PEGI rating only have a plain black strip in the background. This, it seems, is the one that could be vulnerable to the apparent flashlight trick.

However, I haven't managed to track down anybody reporting that they've fallen victim to a stolen code. Most retailers keep their games behind locked glass cases, so a prospective code thief would probably have to buy the game, hope that it's a black background version, get an unusually powerful flashlight, shine it in, and then convince the retailer to take the game back for a refund in order for anyone to fall afoul of the potential scam.

Is that a level of trouble anyone's willing to go to in order to play GTA 6 for free? Well, yeah, I guess so. But it's also not an issue unique to GTA's code-in-box release – I've had a few occasions where I've purchased a new, "sealed" copy of a traditional physical game only to find that someone had carefully snuck the disc out of the package and returned it to the retailer where I eventually bought it.

And, well, if you're that worried, you can just buy the game digitally. Yeah, I know, I'm the exact kind of sicko who bought the physical version to have a box on my shelf and a poster on my wall, but it's not as if there's a real difference between getting the box and just doing a digital GTA 6 pre-order. Now, if there was actually a map in the box, that might be a different story.

#3784. Activision cracking down on popular Call of Duty: Warzone app that basically constituted cheating

"Lobby shopping" is what Call of Duty: Warzone players have been calling the ability to check the skill level of players in a lobby prior to joining it, enabling them to pass on those that include a lot of tough competition.

There are several ways players, notably Twitch streamers and content creators, have been able to do that over the years. But the use of one app in particular - Warzone Agent - has been considered by many to be cheating, and Activision is finally doing something about it.

Alongside the launch of Modern Warfare 4's version of Warzone and the game's first season of post-launch content, Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet has announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

"Yesterday, we began taking action against Warzone Agent, a paid, unauthorised third party tool that lets users lobby shop in Warzone," the developer revealed in a post on X. "Ricochet anti-cheat will block players attempting to load the software and instruct them to unload it before accessing multiplayer."

Having the ability to cherrypick the lobby with the lowest-skilled players possible bypasses the game's matchmaking algorithm, potentially ruining the game for the dozens of other players in the match. Historically, content creators have used the app (and other methods) to post impressive kill records.

The developer added in a follow-up message that: "Using unauthorised software to manipulate the player experience violates Activision terms of use and leaves your account and hardware subject to enforcement." The language seems to stop just short of outright confirming those players using Warzone Agent will be banned.

As part of this crackdown, Ricochet reiterated its stance on boosting - artificially increasing (or decreasing) one's skill rating - saying that it too is considered cheating. "Receiving a boost, having another player log in to boost your account, or purchasing a boosted account are all against policy," the developer said.

"Boosting services flood lobbies with low effort accounts used to farm XP and complete challenges. Those accounts can later be sold as Ranked Play ready, directly feeding the cheating marketplace."

More than 20,000 boosting-related accounts have been removed since the launch of Modern Warfare 4, according to the developer, and Ricochet will "continue to apply pressure" in this area.

The quality of multiplayer was a particular highlight in Eurogamer's review of Modern Warfare 4, in which Dom Peppiatt lauded the complexity of weapon handling, which works without taking away from accessibility of the gunplay.

Ex-Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang has again been summoned to United States Congress to speak with lawmakers. On the agenda are national security issues that may have arisen from his, and his company's, relationship with MegaSpeed, a Singaporean-registered company at the centre of a debate about China's access to high-performance GPUs; possible interference with US export control investigations; and chip smuggling.

“As reports continue to come to light regarding Jensen Huang, Nvidia, and Megaspeed, there are clear national security concerns that need to be addressed immediately,” US committee chairmen Mast, Moolenaar, and Crawford say about the letters summoning Huang, Nvidia's General Counsel Tim Teter, and Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler to Congress.

“We need to know the full extent to which our national security has been put at risk," the chairmen say.

This meetings are to take place with the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, House Select Committee on the CCP, and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. Huang and Teter's meetings are described as 'closed-door transcribed interviews', taking place on December 1 and December 2, respectively. Both parties are threatened with subpoena to force their attendance if they do not comply with the request. Under Secretary Kessler's invitation is described as a "hearing" and is much more amicable.

It's a marked change in tone for Huang compared to a letter sent by the chairmen prior to his resignation from Nvidia, which simply asked him to offer an alternative date should he not be able to attend. That focused more on Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy and former managing director of MegaSpeed.

The letter to Nvidia's counsel Teter outlines the more recent concerns of the committees:

"This letter is to request your appearance for a closed-door transcribed interview on December 2, 2026, regarding AI chip smuggling, adversary military use of Nvidia products, and recent public reports regarding Nvidia's interference in U.S. export control policies and investigations, including those involving MegaSpeed."

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

If that's not a big headache for Nvidia, its former CEO has also been called in for a hearing with the US Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs. This hearing is led by chairman senator Tim Scott.

Scott also calls on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to attend a hearing. Lutnick is Kessler's boss, and has reportedly accepted Scott's invitation. Lutnick has come under some scrutiny as to whether he was too soft on, or protected, Nvidia.

Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology. I am requesting that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee. The American people deserve answers.November 13, 2026

And the democrats readying to take over Congress next year aren't happy with Huang, Nvidia or the supposed risks to national security, either.

There needs to be a full accounting of Jensen Huang, Nvidia, Megaspeed, and the Trump administration's actions in light of serious national security risks. We don't need to wait for Dems to take over Congress in January. At a minimum, Congress needs to be briefed immediately.November 12, 2026

Huang's hearing with the Banking Committee is set to be public, taking place on December 3. It covers the "significant national security concerns" raised by recent reports, according to the letter.

The BBC reports that Huang is willing to appear before Congress.

Every year, the internet debates when it’s an appropriate time to start decorating for the holiday season. Christmas aficionados claim November 1st as the official start of the winter holiday season, while the less festive don’t want to see a single Christmas decoration until after Thanksgiving. It’s no secret that the Kardashian family loves Christmas, so it’s really no surprise that Khloé falls into team decorate immediately after Halloween.

Last year, the mom of two opted for a more subdued approach to her holiday decorating, happily participating in the “naked Christmas tree” trend. However, this year Kardashian has swung the other way, leaning into opulence by creating a truly extra outdoor holiday display. Of course, she took to Instagram to share the bright display with her 291 million followers.

Khloé must be a fan of one of the best Christmas movies ever, Christmas Vacation, because she went full Clark Griswold on her home. Just like the beloved family patriarch, the reality star chose to decorate with elegant white twinkling lights, wrapping them around the landscaping around her home, and several outdoor Christmas trees brought in for the display. I didn’t think anything would top Kim Kardashian’s hallway of Christmas trees, but this display definitely does.

In addition to the gorgeous twinkling trees, the lights adorn her home. Unlike the iconic Griswold house, Kardashian opted for a neater approach to the holiday lights on her home, using them to illuminate the roofline and frame the windows and doorways.

She referred to the choice as “Gingerbread style” because the lights look like icing on a gingerbread house. I’ve never heard of the style before, but now that a Kardashian is endorsing it, I’m sure we’ll see it pop up more and more, especially amongst other Christmas-obsessed celebrities like Reese Witherspoon, who always dazzles with her decorations.

Khloé Kardashian Reveals The Blunt Note She And Her Family Got Before Filming KUWTK’s First Season

The Good American founder did make it clear that she had help creating the winter wonderland display, crediting The Christmas Brothers for the installation. They definitely deserve a round of applause, and maybe a reality TV show of their own so we can see how much work goes into creating such an extra but gorgeous display.

Christmas isn’t the only winter holiday Khloé and the rest of the Kardashian-Jenner fam are prepping for, though. They also have to get ready for “SKIMSmas”! The underwear, loungewear, and shapewear line is a partnership between the five sisters, and the holiday season is their busiest time of year, with the girls often reuniting for campaign videos announcing the opening of the holiday shop.

Unfortunately, SKIMSmas has been a slight disappointment for fans this year thanks to a disappointing advent calendar. Thankfully, SKIMS has issued refunds to all the affected buyers, so Christmas is saved. I’m sure all will be forgotten as soon as we get more photos of Khloé and the rest of her family’s epic holiday displays and outfits.

#3780. Over A Third Of Game Developers Have Lost A Job In The Last Two Years, Bleak Report Finds

Over a third of all game developers were laid off over the last two years, claims a sobering report from Game Developers Conference (GDC) about the state of the industry. The report surveyed developers from around the world about a number of hot-button topics, from job losses to AI, to get a picture of the industry as we enter perhaps its most unstable era in recent memory.

In response to a question asking about layoffs over the past 24 months, 34 percent of respondents worldwide said they had lost a job in the games industry. U.S.-based developers were even more likely to be laid off at 39 percent. Itâs a trend thatâs only going up, the report adds, noting an increase every time the question has been asked over the past three years. Even those who are employed are not exactly in stable work: only 50 percent of U.S. respondents are employed full-time (down 9 percent).

Of those who have lost their jobsâroughly 900 respondents according to GDCâsome have faced multiple layoffs in that period. 17 percent of this group were laid off twice, with three percent facing three or more layoffs in a 24-month period. With fewer jobs available, over 54 percent say they have not yet found another job, while it took 15 percent of this group over six months to find new work. The results of those finding a job are mixed, too: nine percent ended up finding work outside games, while four percent started their own studio or company.

It paints a worrisome picture. The wealth of experience these developers possess is now at risk of being lost for good. It also hurts morale, with over half of respondents (51 percent) strongly agreeing to the statement that they were âconcerned about my future in the game industry.â A total of 73 percent of respondents at least slightly disagreed with the statement that they were âhopeful about where the game industry is headed.â

The sentiment across all responses in the survey noted developers held pessimistic feelings about the future of the industry and their own prospects within it. With consolidation and AI rampant, itâs hard to blame them. Speaking of AI, while there is a concern that the tech will replace jobs, its usage across the industry remains far lower than in other tech fields. Questioned on AI usage in their development work, 60 percent stated they do not use it. Older developers tend to use it more than younger developers, with significantly more men than women using the tools (45 percent vs 33 percent). Its usage in both indie and premium games was under one-third, with higher usage only being seen by devs working on free-to-play games (58 percent) and mobile-only games (70 percent).

These results go against the conceptions that AI usage is more common than is often disclosed, with a number of developers noting their company either discourages (11 percent) or entirely prohibits (23 percent) AI usage in any capacity. Those who use it, however, are using it very often, most often daily. Concerns over the middling quality of vibecoded releases often give AI a negative reputation, never mind the ways players are often quick to condemn its use. It doesnât help that 56 percent of people see it as having a negative impact on the industry.

The survey, released as part of GDC’s yearly recap of the industry, also touches on topics of working hours and the impact of work on mental health, all pointing toward an unstable time for the game industry. The instability is leading to less advocacy for improving that working situation as wellâwhile support for unions remains high at 80 percent, because layoffs are so frequent and the difficulty of finding a new job so high, the interest in joining unions has actually fallen. People involved in games still love them, and find immense satisfaction from making and playing them. There just isnât much hope surrounding their future right now.

#3779. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under investigation after admitting affair with alleged Chinese spy in company-wide email

"There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Nvidia's board of directors has launched an investigation into its own CEO Jensen Huang, after a report by the New York Times claimed he had been participating in an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Huang admitted to having an affair in a company-wide statement, apologising to his wife as well as to Nvidia employees. Following this acknowledgement, independent investigators are looking into whether or not he's been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Per the New York Times article, the alleged spy was named as Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. Jensen Huang wrote in his internal letter: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

With regard to security concerns surrounding the CEO of US-based company Nvidia potentially sharing information with a spy, Huang confirmed that the Nvidia board of directors had initiated an investigation. He added: "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully." The Nvidia board has said it has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

Huang will remain CEO of Nvidia while the investigation is conducted. The New York Times report also claimed that US government officials did not believe Huang knew of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China.

Following the internal letter from Jensen Huang, Nvidia stock took a tumble from $162bn to $150bn. Nvidia, a juggernaut in the video game hardware industry, is also a key player in the global generative AI industry, which is currently carrying the US economy as other sectors struggle. The company is responsible for AI technology like DLSS 5, which generates lighting, shadows and more using generative AI.

Concerns around the Chinese AI sector passing the American industry has been a core argument against AI development slowdown or regulation, and it's also why Huang's affair may be a matter of national interest.

There's an A-bomb, but no F-bombs in Godzilla Minus Zero.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I've told this story before on this website, but my dad took me to see the very R-rated Terminator 2: Judgment Day when I was only 8 years old.

Now, while I will say that it was a truly transformative experience - the opening scene alone was definitely the most mind-blowing thing I had ever seen in my entire life up to that point - my dad instantly regretted taking me the moment they started dropping F-bomb after F-bomb.

So, with that in mind, I didn't want to make the same mistake as my dad. That’s why when I heard that Godzilla Minus Zero was rated R, I made sure to watch it first BEFORE I took my 9-year-old son. After watching it (it was amazing, by the way), I decided that it was indeed okay to take him. Here's why.

My son is no stranger to bad words. We don't say them in our household, but the kids at his school curse all the time (and my son likely does, too, when he's with his friends. That's what I did when I was his age, anyway). That said, I don't really want him to see an R-rated movie with lots of swearing, since I know people can be quite creative with HOW they curse in movies. Granted, I wasn't particularly worried about cursing in a Godzilla movie (especially since there were subtitles), but I wanted to be on the safe side.

Well, I can report that there are NO bad words in this movie. In fact, the dialogue is no worse than it was in Godzilla Minus One, which I took my then 6-year-old son to see when it first came out. So, the next thing I worry about in an R-rated film is nudity or sexual content. Now, I wasn't TOO concerned that there would be any nudity in a Godzilla movie, but again, I didn't understand WHY this movie had to be rated R.

Well, again, I can report that there is nothing to worry about in this regard, either, as there is no nudity or sexual content whatsoever. In fact, the only time there was anything questionable was BEFORE the movie, as there were two red band trailers in my showing - one for a movie called Karōshi, and another for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, the latter of which had a few F-bombs in it. So, that was something I prepared my son for when I saw the movie a second time and took him with me. The trailers!

Now, here's the thing about violence when it comes to my son - I'm not too worried about it as long as it's FANTASY violence. For example, my son has been playing T for Teen games ever since he was five, with his first T-rated game being Shadow of the Colossus. Since then, he's played several other T-rated games, and I've never been upset with them because they're not realistic.

Mind you, I've been a Mortal Kombat megafan since 1992, so I only thought it fair to allow my son to play video games with moderate amounts of violence. So, when I saw Godzilla Minus Zero for the first time, I thought the violence was okay for my son. In fact, it’s rather tame in comparison to something like Bloodborne, which is an M-rated game that my son is currently playing.

There are two scenes in the movie that I was slightly worried about, though. One involves a family burnt to a crisp by an atomic bomb, and another scene involves Godzilla literally being ripped to pieces by King Ghidorah. Besides those two scenes, I honestly don't see why this movie is rated R in the first place. That's why I had no problem taking my son to see Godzilla Minus Zero. Besides, for a first-time R-rated film, it definitely could have been worse. I mean, it could have been Terminator 2: Judgment Day.

Rich is a Jersey boy, through and through. He graduated from Rutgers University (Go, R.U.!), and thinks the Garden State is the best state in the country. That said, he’ll take Chicago Deep Dish pizza over a New York slice any day of the week. Don’t hate. When he’s not watching his two kids, he’s usually working on a novel, watching vintage movies, or reading some obscure book.

#3776. Anticipated Warhammer 40K tactical RPG Dark Heresy gets a release date

Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says.

Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review.

Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure.

There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch.

Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect. That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider, and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.

"Reddit does not receive a cut of any purchases made through the buy it now button on product pages."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A couple of days ago I reported that Reddit is rolling out reviews for different products, informed by Redditors' thoughts and molded by AI into into dedicated review pages for these products. Given Reddit says "many reviews also include images, prices, and purchase links", I wondered whether Reddit would be making any affiliate money from this. Well, I now have an answer: the company tells us it will not receive a cut.

In an email sent to me, a Reddit rep explains: "Reddit Reviews is an organic experience, and Reddit does not receive a cut of any purchases made through the buy it now button on product pages."

Not that I would have had a massive problem with this—PC Gamer earns affiliate revenue itself—but I suppose it's good to know there won't be a financial incentive there at least in that respect. And it does at least tie in with the aimed "organic" nature of Reddit in general.

I was also concerned that users might review-bomb products they don't like, or that companies could use bots to positively influence reviews for their own products. Reddit reassures us about that, too:

"Platform-wide, we are taking numerous steps to prevent and enforce against inauthentic content."

That's certainly more reassuring than nothing, but we'll have to see how it goes in practice. AI and bot farms make the modern landscape tricky business, and I'm sure there must already be actors out there giving pretty convincing supposedly first-personal reviews of products on different platforms, whether to bolster or undermine these products.

#3773. How to find a Guild in WoW Forever

No Guild Finder (so far) isn't stopping WoW: Forever players from finding (or even making) the perfect Guild

Guilds return in World of Warcraft: Forever, and Blizzard wants to recapture the excitement of hopping into the game and dragging your guildmates to the occasional raid, a good leveling session, or the plain old shenanigans. While guilds are already a staple in most MMOs and other versions of WoW, it’s still refreshing to see Forever return with a classic iteration of a staple social experience.

But since Forever is indeed a remake of Classic, it also comes with the sheer difficulty of finding a Guild you could be a part of. There’s really no way to tell if a Guild is available for applications, or maybe if a Guild is strictly friends-only. Then again, there are creative ways where you can score a Guild membership for your character.

Historically, WoW players have always been able to find Guilds through the Guild Finder, launched back in Cataclysm, as well as the improved Guild & Communities Finder back in 2019. Forever being a remake of the OG WoW means going back to a time where none of these tools existed, so it’s back to “manual” searching for WoW: Forever players.

As of writing, there are no WoW: Forever add-ons specifically to help find Guilds in the game. Sites like CurseForge do have a plethora of add-ons that help with Guild management, but that’s after you make your Guild.

Cataclysm launched the original Guild Finder back in 2011, so players had around seven years of finding guilds with no built-in tool to help them. Therefore, WoW: Forever players can also resort to old-fashioned ways of finding prospective Guilds.

Even without the Guild Finder, WoW: Forever players have a plethora of social avenues to form communities and find like-minded players for their Guilds. Forums and community messaging apps are perfect for guild recruitment, especially if they have dedicated group chats for Forever. Example avenues are:

Reddit and Discord are already great places to stay connected with fellow players or even get tips on things like PvP and builds, so it’s no surprise they are also great platforms to find Guilds to join.

There’s nothing wrong jumping to and from Guilds if you feel like the one you’re in doesn’t really suit your needs anymore. But to avoid those awkward situations when you do need to type “/gquit” in the chat, then remember these when joining:

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Maybe you don’t want to be part of a Guild. Maybe you found some Guilds taking the game too seriously and you want something chill, or some Guilds might be “too” chill for your liking. That’s probably when you should consider making your own Guild.

If you want to create your own Guild, it has to be something certified by your Faction as 100% legit. This is quite unlike other MMOs where you can just make a Guild easy peasy, or just pay some currency to get the privilege. Instead, you need to get something called a Guild Charter.

To do this, head to your capital city. Ask a guard to help you locate your Guild Master. From here, you can ask them for a Guild Charter, and they’ll sell it to you for 10 Silver.

Be careful if you’re doing this purchase if you’re low-level, since that 10 Silver is already the current life savings of other characters. But once you’ve decided you really want to become a future guild founder, then proceed with the purchase and type in your Guild Name.

This won’t stop there, though. Before your Guild actually becomes legit, you need to find 10 Signatures first.

Unlike other MMOs, WoW: Forever takes a page from Classic’s rulebook and demands Signatures from other players to co-found your Guild. As with Classic, you also need 10 (!!!) Signatures in your Guild Charter. And if you’re not playing with friends who are ready to be your co-founders, it’s not easy to convince random people to just hop in and join someone’s Guild.

Once you find a player willing to help, you just right-click their name and ask them for their Signature. A prompt will appear on their end where they can sign your Guild Charter.

When you finally get your Signatures, you must rush back to your capital city and turn in the signed Guild Charter. Only then do you get your guild. But first things first, how exactly do you find Signatures?

Before you run off to Stormwind to grab that Guild Charter, just remember that creating a Guild in Forever does have its fair set of limitations. Huddle with your prospective guildmates and remember the following:

After you create your Guild, you practically have access to a mini-Faction within the Forever experience. As the leader, you (and a select few you appoint) have access to some of the Guild’s core settings. You can adjust these at any time, but the basics you should pay attention to are the following:

You might recall the suggestion to go to Discord to find a guild to join, or maybe even find potential guildmates. That’s because you can actually connect your WoW: Forever account to your Discord account as well. Doing this is pretty simple, and it’s all done from your settings:

First, you need to connect your Discord to your Battle.net account. To do this, go to your Discord account and click “User Settings.”

Under “Connected Apps,” you will see “Add a new connection,” and you can click the Battle.net icon there.

It will open Battle.net, where you can click “Continue,” and it will send you back to Discord, where you can “Authorize” the connection.

After that, you will be redirected to your settings, where you can confirm the connection.

Back in your WoW: Forever session, go to your “Options” and find “Social” under “Gameplay” or via the search.

It will show the Enable Discord Functionality toggle. Connect so you can link your Discord to your specific WoW account.

Below that setting is an option to choose how your name is displayed in the chat connected to Discord. It could be your Discord Global Name or your Last Online Character Name.

This part is best done if you’re the owner of the Guild, so you can set this up from scratch. Over in the “Guilds & Communities” tab, you can go to your “Guild Control” and check out Discord Settings.

From there, you can choose which Discord Server you want to connect to your Guild. And after that, you can select which specific channel you want to add to your Forever Guild.

When you link the two, the Discord channel overrides the Guild Chat by default. But there’s an option to separate the Discord chat as a separate channel from the Guild Chat.

Now, all your messages in WoW: Forever in that specific chat can be seen live on Discord. Likewise, messages from Discord will be seen back in WoW: Forever, with a nifty Discord icon to denote that the message has been sent from Discord specifically but read in-game.

While it’s possible to just separate your Discord chat from your Guild Chat, it might be economical to fix things over on Discord so that you have a dedicated guild channel for in-game players. You can lock that channel as view-only to non-players, so only guild members can actually chat there.

#3771. Hollow Knight Silksong physical editions mention multiple "free content packs" incoming, and call Sea of Sorrow a "giant expansion"

More than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong are finally arriving on players' doorsteps. It's the same brilliant and sometimes thrillingly cruel Metroidvania Eurogamer gave five stars to, except this time a pack-in booklet seemingly reveals the existence of multiple "free content packs" alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC.

Hollow Knight: Silksong's physical editions were originally set to be delivered from 10th November, but some early handovers have given us a peek inside the box. Redditor Me_975 posted pictures of their Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, and there's a few interesting tidbits tucked away - most notably in the manual's chapter on Content Packs.

"The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet reads. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!"

Developer Team Cherry confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support last year, but remained pretty tight-lipped about what exactly that would look like. The indie outfit then announced the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow expansion, though we now have proper confirmation there's more content packs still to come, which shouldn't be a huge shocker considering all the free post-launch love Hollow Knight (the first one) received.

Speaking of Sea of Sorrow, that's mentioned here too: "In the first giant expansion, voyage across and beneath a salt-stricken ocean brimming with mystery and menace."

Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - time's a-ticking, Team Cherry. Still no release date so far, but the booklet does say it's "Coming Soon." Of course, Team Cherry are quite infamous for working on games until they balloon wildly out of control. After all, Silksong was once upon a time intended to be a Hollow Knight DLC, but with games this detailed, I can't really complain about waiting a little extra.

If you are interested in owning Silksong physically, it comes with a big map of Pharloom and the rest of the booklet also includes some really lovely art seemingly ripped straight from the game, as well.

Ain't nobody buying gaming CPUs right now.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Intel appears to have gained market share from AMD in a rare turnaround for the company. The red team's chips have been in the lead in performance and popularity for many years now, and frankly, they still are. That's what weird about this one: AMD may have lost ground because it makes the best CPUs for gaming.

The latest Q3, 2026 data from market researchers Mercury Research suggests an increase in market share for desktop CPUs of 5.1%. Now, considering AMD has fought tooth and nail for a decade to increase its share to around 35% as of Q2, 2026, dropping down to just 29.9% in the following three months marks a gargantuan lurch back towards Intel.

Our pick for the best gaming CPU is the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and many other AMD chips make up our recommendations. While we do recommend the Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus due to its surprisingly low price tag and plenty of cores, I wouldn't go as far as believing any Arrow Lake chip has been key to turning around Intel's fortunes among gamers. The architecture struggles to keep up with AMD's latest in gaming, and it is built on a dead-end platform—Nova Lake chips are expected soon on a different motherboard socket.

The increase in market share is almost too big to be believed, which is certainly one theory as to what's going on. A rounding error or errant data—though Mercury Research have been pretty locked in in the past. Both Intel and AMD cite their numbers when it makes them look good.

Mercury Research put its hands up to say it isn't totally sure what happened, either:

"It's difficult to know the driver of this for sure, but we speculate that due to the lower mobile CPU demand, Intel could allocate more products to the desktop market, which normally sees a significant demand increase in the third quarter, and Intel had been under-supplying this market earlier in 2026.

"AMD, however, did not appear to have a seasonal increase, which resulted in Intel having a very large sequential and on-year gain in desktop CPU market share," Mercury Research says.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

The other theory presented by the market research company is that AMD has "greater exposure" to gaming—by way of offering the best gaming chips.

"We believe another component to Intel's gains here is AMD's greater exposure to the PC gaming market, which has suffered due to supply constraints of gaming GPUs."

Mercury Research say 'supply constraints' when it's more like prices are so absurd for GPUs, RAM, and storage as to be comical, which lends to a general malaise among gamers to building a new PC. But, either way, this theory makes some sense. Intel still holds huge sway with system builders and OEMs, the likes of which are buying up both new and old (DDR4-compatible) chips for cheap systems. And not just gaming systems, which we see both Intel and AMD get a fairly decent share of during our weekly trawling for gaming PC deals.

AMD also admitted it is has a supply deficit at the moment; demand is outstripping supply. It's working to close that deficit, but what it means by that is grow its datacentre chip business more in the coming months and years. After all, AMD is a datacentre company now.

I wouldn't mistake Intel 'gaining market share' as a healthy sign for the company or the wider industry. Mercury Research suggested desktop CPU volumes had seen a "large drop" in Q2, 2026, and both Intel and AMD are said to have seen more than a 10% drop in shipments for mobile chips in Q3, 2026. They're fighting for scraps in the consumer market.

Intel has seen a momentous share price drop as of late due to weak sale expectations due to a crappy PC market, but AMD is set to beat Intel for total revenue by the end of year.

3. Best mid-range: Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus

#3767. God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind

God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics. About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2, a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs, however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases, analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Hunger Games movies became a sensation upon their release, with the public obsessed with the book-to-screen adaptations. Luckily for fans, we're returned to Panem thanks to Suzanne Collins' prequels. We're very close to the release of Francis Lawrence's Sunrise on the Reaping, which tells the story of Haymitch's Games. But should moviegoers read the novel before heading to theaters? I asked that very question to both the director and star, Joseph Zada.

What we know about Sunrise on the Reaping depends on if you read the source material, but fans are preparing for a heartbreaking story about the second Quarter Quell. I had the privilege of speaking with Zada about the blockbuster and asked him if fans should read the book or go in blind. He told me:

I think, I think actually maybe if you have read the book, because you know it's coming the whole time. That's always such a horrible feeling when you know what's coming. I brought that into the last bit of the film. It's like my character in the back of his head knows what's, what's coming. Horrible. Horrible. But I also think, yeah, it would be a bit shocking having no idea coming back. Either or. Each their own. You don't have to be a fan either to watch this.

There's no correct way to watch the new Hunger Games flick, but those who read Sunrise on the Reaping know exactly what tragedies are coming. That's how I watched the film, and as soon as certain doomed characters appeared, my stomach dropped, knowing when they would die and how. You can see my conversation with the East of Eden star below:

A post shared by CinemaBlend (@cinemablend)

Of course, I had to ask the movie's director this same question. Francis Lawrence has a long history with the franchise, having directed five out of the six Hunger Games movies. He weighed in on whether he thinks one should go into Sunrise on the Reaping with or without knowledge of what happened in its corresponding novel. He told me:

What I like about this story is that I think, quite honestly, you could come, this could be your entry point into the series. And I think you could come in fresh, don't know anything about the movies, go and see this thing. You start, you get behind this kid that you love, and you go on this ride, and you start to meet these characters, and then you could go out from there. 'Cause I think a lot of the times people think, 'Oh, you have to have this to then be able to sort of look at and understand who the young people are.' But I think you can go the other way too. But I think you can, you could go into this fresh not knowing anything. And not even having read the book, and I think you'll have a very emotional experience.

He's not wrong. While there will be fans who have read and watched every single Hunger Games story, newbies can also walk in fresh to Sunrise on the Reaping. Any essential exposition is dropped to help those moviegoers, while the hardcore fandom will watch the prequel with the knowledge of what came before and after Haymitch's games.

Of course, there are plenty of moments in this new movie that longtime fans will especially appreciate. Namely the spot-on impressions of Woody Harrelson and Jeffrey Wright that are being performed by Joseph Zada and Kelvin Harrison Jr. respectively. Conversely, folks who read the book are burdened with knowing what happens to the characters in the new Hunger Games movie, while casual fans will be able to be shocked by all of the new movie's twists.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will hit theaters on November 20th as part of the 2026 movie release list. Meanwhile, fans can rewatch all of the previous movies with their Hulu subscription.

I'm Commander Shepard and this is my favorite video on the internet.

This N7 Day was the first without developer BioWare around, but fans of the Mass Effect series didn't let 7th November go by quietly. The community managed to get several notable Mass Effect actors to lend their voice to the increasingly loud 'SaveMassEffect' movement.

In the weeks since BioWare's shock closure and Mass Effect Universe's cancellation, the community-organised We Are Mass Effect group have put up billboards in Times Square, a mobile billboard outside BioWare Edmonton's former office and much more while directing attention to an online petition.

Today is a very special day for Mass Effect fans. We've worked incredibly hard to bring together most of the original Mass Effect trilogy's voice cast to share a very important message with you. We need to #SaveMassEffect. https://t.co/FOp0qp4wBI

And for the series' annual celebration, the group managed to get a sizable portion of the Mass Effect cast to join in. Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, original trilogy composer Sam Hulick, Garrus' Brandon Keener, Jack's Courtnay Taylor, Tali'Zorah's Ash Sroka, Thane's Keythe Farley and many more all showed up in a two-minute video to help potentially salvage the series - sometimes in character.

"When we heard about the formal closing of Boware, I felt weirdly hopeful," Hale said in a separate interview with IGN. "I can't explain it. I just got so weirdly hopeful. My first thought, of course, was for the devs and all the people. And then I just closed my eyes and crossed my fingers and I said, 'I feel something's possible. You know, something's really possible.'"

The other half of Commander Shepard, Mark Meer, noted that "this didn't all just happen in the last 10 days." Near yearly layoffs at EA had slowly trimmed multiple BioWare teams down, sometimes even affecting studio veterans who had been at the company for decades.

"A lot of senior writers within the last year or two were let go. People who had been there from the very beginning. Again, people who had built that company from the ground up, who built the bones of it, who made those games that had captured people so much right back from the 1990s," Meer said.

TSMC, the juggernaut that produces roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips, has discovered a data leak said to contain over 46,000 employee records, according to Seeking Alpha.

The company made a Form 6-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday, stating: "TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization. Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised."

The company says the info has been verified to match data "stored in the system services of a cloud service provider," although said provider is not named. TSMC says it has informed those impacted by the breach and is providing support, and has also engaged with the cloud service vendor, investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency to "ascertain the facts and take necessary actions."

Taiwanese outlet United Daily News reports that hackers were allegedly offering the employee records on an underground forum for the princely sum of three bitcoin, in exchange for 6.9 GB worth of private data.

The outlet also says that, "according to information online" (via machine translation), hackers were also selling what appears to be TSMC employee data on other forums, releasing a small sample which is said to contain a vast array of personal details, including national ID numbers, addresses, and banking information.

TSMC has confirmed in its statement that the leaked data is unrelated to the company's operations, or customer-related information.

This isn't the first time TSMC has been in the headlines in relation to cybersecurity. Back in 2023, ransomware outfit LockBit attempted to extort the company for $70 million after a claimed hack.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

TSMC denied it had been directly hacked, revealing in a statement that IT hardware supplier Kinmax Technology had been the victim of a "cybersecurity incident" instead, which "led to the leak of information pertinent to server initial setup and configuration." Kinmax also released a statement at the time confirming the breach.

Being such a large and wealthy company at the heart of the tech supply chain, it's no surprise that hackers are keen to gain any details on TSMC if they can. In both these cases, it seems that TSMC's own systems remained secure, but an outside party may have let the side down.

Regardless, I doubt it's the last major data leak I'll be writing about before 2026 is out. This year has been characterised by cybersecurity incidents left, right and centre, and in this every-more-interconnected world, it seems even some of the most security-conscious companies are far from immune.

#3760. GTA 6 pre-orders are tracking "well above expectations" and the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two, says CEO Strauss Zelnick

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick noted that pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking "far above expectations", and is certain that soon "numbers will speak for themselves" when it comes to the game.

Zelnick also promised GTA Online and GTA 5 will continue to receive updates in order to support the "nearly 235 million" units sold to date across "an unprecedented three console generations". The GTA series as a whole has, to date, sold over 480 million units. Karl Statoff, president at Take-Two, adds the launch of GTA 6 will be a "defining moment for the company and global entertainment industry". Zelnick adds, later in a question and answer session, that he expects GTA 6 to "set a new baseline" for Take-Two. "The future's really bright across the board," he notes.

For the next quarter, Take-Two expects to deliver $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion - with "recurrent consumer spending" to raise by 12 percent, driven by "the groundbreaking release" of Grand Theft Auto 6, and expects to see "significant growth for the Grand Theft Auto series", driven by sales of - specifically - Grand Theft Auto 6's Ultimate Edition, which includes add-on content, and that most people are pre-ordering at its $100 price point. That bonus $20 between the $80 base edition and the Ultimate Edition is counted as "recurrent consumer spending", as is part of that massive bump the company has seen.

It also seems that we will see more GTA games - or content, at least - sooner than expected. "We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade." It's a vague comment, but assumedly the work done on the engine and backend of GTA 6 means we'll see more content arriving in shorter order than we're used to for the series. This is per an article published by IGN in line with the earning's call going live.

Elsewhere in the earnings call, Take-Two referred to its current setup with its mobile, sports, 'core new IP' and 'core existing IP' as "the strongest development pipeline in the company's history". In terms of new IP, Zelnick directed investors to consider the launches of incoming projects like Ken Levine's mysterious Judas and Project Ethos (which we don't know too much about yet, other than it's billed as a "roguelike hero shooter"). For core IP, 8 sequels and 7 remakes, remasters, and platform extensions.

Buoyed by these plans, Zelnick outlines that he believes that fiscal year 2027 "will be a historic year for Take-Two" as the company is buoyed by "recent and upcoming releases". No prizes for what that's referring to. If you're curious about what sort of numbers we may be looking at here, all you need to do is cast your mind back to 2014, where you will remember GTA 5 made $1bn in just three days.

#3759. Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic is ‘at the last stage of production,’ Neil Druckmann says

Druckmann finally reveals some new details for Naughty Dog's next game.

Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is Naughty Dog’s latest game, but aside from a few teasers, we haven’t really seen much of the game at all. Despite the clandestine approach, the game is actually “at the last stage of production,” according to Naughty Dog’s chief Neil Druckmann.

Speaking on Revenge Of’s Comic Creators Block Party podcast, Druckmann said Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is “at the last stage of production,” where “we can play it, and we’re refining and polishing it,” but did not reveal too many details about the game’s plot or setting outside of saying it’s Naughty Dog’s venture into science fiction.

Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is in the final stage of production according to Neil Druckmann.He describes it as a combination of Jak and Daxter, Uncharted, and The Last of Us:"We used to have another game franchise called Jak & Daxter […] And with this one, we really…

The choice of sci-fi as the setting came from a desire to build something less grounded and more epic in scale, which, as Druckmann explains, wasn’t really possible with The Last of Us and Uncharted. However, the director said some TLOU and Uncharted DNA definitely went into the creation of Intergalactic, with that game being “a combination” of Jack & Dexter and these two mentioned IPs. Specifically, Druckmann says the studio took Uncharted‘s pulp action, TLOU‘s drama, and Jack & Dexter‘s science-fantasy and smashed them together to form this new and exciting adventure.

“We really wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems. Like, can we sustain the kind of cinematic storytelling we’re used to telling and go even deeper with gameplay,”

“We really wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems. Like, can we sustain the kind of cinematic storytelling we’re used to telling and go even deeper with gameplay?” Druckmann said.

Anime played a crucial role as inspiration for Intergalactic, the director said, naming Evangelion and Akira as key examples, and not just because of their futuristic style. Both of these anime have intricate and complex philosophical ideas which are approached in a very strange, disconnected, and weird way, or, as Druckmann puts it, they take you on a “wild ride,” and that is exactly what Naughty Dog aims to do in Intergalactic.

Druckmann added that the studio plans to reveal more of the story and the gameplay for Intergalactic next year, and that players will be surprised to see what the game is actually about.

#3758. The 25th Anniversary Xbox Is So Impossible To Find Even GameStop Is Selling It For $5,000

Microsoft just made its 25th Anniversary Xbox Series X console available, and it was on sale for approximately 0.3 seconds. Scalpers swooped in and bought the lot in the most tediously predictable way, with presumably one or two legitimate customers squeaking in alongside them. And in the midst of all this, GameStop managed to list the $900 machine for $4,950. In fact, even the direct link from Microsoft’s own site will take you to a page offering it for that price.

The special edition Series X is made in a translucent green to match the design of the original Xbox from 2001, and is intended to sell for an already incredibly steep $900. (Bear in mind this is just the 1TB model.) It comes with a modern controller in matching see-through green, with both machine and controller engraved with “XBOX 25,” and you get a copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved thrown in too. However, none of this justifies a $5000 price.

It’s deeply peculiar that in these times, when pretty much any special edition of anything gaming-related sells out instantaneously, Microsoft wouldn’t have instituted some sort of limitations on how the console could be bought. Instead, the green machines were in stock for a matter of seconds before being listed as “sold out” or “coming soon.” Or in the case of Walmart, just entirely delisted from the store like it never existed.

GameStop still seems to have stock, however! At the time of this writing, I was able to add the $4,950 X25 edition to my basket, where it then added $7.99 in shipping and handling, and another $353.26 in tax. A mere $5,311.25!

Gamestop increases preorder prices of the Xbox 25th Console by $500 overnight. byu/plagueislandcc inxbox

Last night Reddit users noticed that GameStop had bumped the pre-order price for the X25 up to $1,500, ahead of it actually going on sale. Now another $3,450 as been tacked on. Why? Our best guess is that this is GameStop attempting to price-match what it’s finding elsewhere for “used” versions, i.e. the scalping prices people are aiming for on secondhand markets. eBay is currently flooded with offers for the machine at around $1,700, and the highest I’ve found is $2,395.95,Â so somehow GameStop is even doubling this.

This very much matches GameStop’s current model for selling PokÃ©mon cards, with the outlet appearing to have become a store-based scalping company for the TCG. MSRP be damned when there are desperate people out there trying to buy its products.
